people.name: Jacob Thornton
people.status: CEO of Pierre Computer Company, which OpenAI agreed to acquire on November 4, 2026.
people.verifiedHow: YC's founder page lists him as Pierre's founder, and OpenAI announced its agreement to acquire Pierre on November 4, 2026.
people.short: Co-created Bootstrap, then built Pierre, the code-review company OpenAI agreed to acquire.
people.signal: Twitter (Bootstrap) → Medium → Bumpers → Coinbase → Pierre → OpenAI deal
people.why: **He connects the open-source web with the next generation of code review.** At Twitter he co-created Bootstrap, the front-end toolkit a huge share of the web was built on, then was an early engineer at Medium. With Ian Ownbey he went on to found Pierre Computer Company, a YC-backed rethink of how teams review code, and on November 4, 2026 OpenAI announced an agreement to acquire it. From Bootstrap to Codex's front door.

people.short: Took a lifelong love of systems into making AI inference provable at Anthropic.

people.why: **He connects decades of developer education with cryptographic proof for AI.** He started Cprogramming.com as a young teenager, studied computer science at Harvard, shipped security software at Liquid Machines and wrote the book Jumping into C++. Work on verifiable inference with 0xPARC and the Field Extension Institute led him to Anthropic in 2026, where on November 2 he co-authored FlashProve, a way to prove which model actually served a response. Trust, but verify the weights.
